title: Negatives and Questions Quiz 6
description: Every question hides a trap: a double negative, an extra helper, inversion or an embedded question.
instructions: Negatives and Questions: Difficult: negatives and questions.
Read each question carefully, then check your answer.
Every question has a trap. Read every word.

questions.question: Which sentence is correct?
options: I didn't see nobody at the party.
I not saw anybody at the party.
I didn't see anybody at the party.
I didn't saw anybody at the party.
questions.explanation: Anybody works with a negative verb, and didn't takes the base form: I didn't see anybody. Watch out: nobody after didn't gives a double negative.

questions.question: 'Hadn't she been waiting long?' is a correct negative question.
questions.explanation: Only had moves, and its short form goes with it: Hadn't she been waiting? Watch out: been and waiting stay after the subject.

questions.question: How long {{1}} he {{2}} (wait) when the bus finally came? Use the past perfect continuous.
questions.explanation: The past perfect continuous question is Had + subject + been + verb-ing. Watch out: only had moves in front of he.

questions.question: Which sentence is correct?
options: Never have I seen such a crowd.
Never I have seen such a crowd.
Never I saw have such a crowd.
Never did I seen such a crowd.
questions.explanation: A negative adverb at the front pulls the helper before the subject: Never have I seen. Watch out: Never I have seen keeps statement order.

questions.question: Which question is correct?
options: Who has my pen taken?
Who has took my pen?
Who taken my pen?
Who has taken my pen?
questions.explanation: Who is the subject, so has stays as the helper and no other helper is added: Who has taken my pen? Watch out: the participle of take is taken, not took.

questions.question: Correct the mistake: Did he had finished before you arrived?
accepted: Had he finished before you arrived?
Had he finished before you arrived
questions.explanation: The past perfect question is Had + subject + participle. Watch out: did and had never go together here.

questions.assertion: In 'Who rang you?', no helper (do / does / did) is needed.
questions.reason: Who is the subject of the verb.
questions.explanation: The reason explains the assertion: who is the subject of rang, so the question needs no helper. Watch out: if who were the object, as in Who did you ring?, did would be needed.

questions.question: If you {{1}} (not / hurry), you will miss the train.
questions.explanation: After if, the present simple is used, including in the negative. Watch out: if you won't hurry is wrong.

questions.question: Which sentences are correct?
options: Hardly had she sat down when it rang.
Isn't she coming?
Doesn't she knows him?
Did you not went home?
questions.explanation: A negative adverb such as hardly pulls had in front of the subject, and a negative question keeps the helper before the subject. Watch out: after doesn't or didn't the verb is in the base form.

questions.question: Put the words in the correct order to make a sentence.
questions.explanation: Seldom is a negative adverb, so the helper have goes before the subject we. Watch out: such a film stays together at the end.

questions.question: Which sentence is correct?
options: I didn't know where was the station.
I didn't know where the station was.
I didn't know where did the station was.
I didn't knew where the station was.
questions.explanation: An indirect question keeps statement order: where the station was. Watch out: did and was do not belong in a statement clause.

questions.question: 'Isn't she coming?' and 'Is she not coming?' have the same meaning.
questions.explanation: Both are negative questions. The full not in the second is more formal. Watch out: in the short form, n't travels in front of the subject with the helper.
